SCGSim is a Python package: it builds the model, writes the solver's input and
reads the results back, but it does not include the solvers. This page installs
SCGSim `3.0.0rc4` and the OrcaPen SC PDK, the component library every example
draws its layout with, in a study project, then says what each extra adds and
what Palace and AEDT need. SCGSim supports Python `>=3.12,<3.14`.

## 1. Install uv and Git

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads). Git lets `uv` fetch SCGSim from the [canonical source repository](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim).

Check: `uv --version` and `git --version` each print an installed version.

## 2. Create the study project {#create-the-project}

<span id="create-the-project-and-add-scgsim"></span>These are the commands of the [home page](../../index.qmd#install): SCGSim at
the tag `v3.0.0rc4` with its `palace` extra, and the PDK at the revision the
examples use.

```bash
uv init --python 3.12 scgsim-study
cd scgsim-study
uv add 'scgsim[palace] @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim.git@v3.0.0rc4' \
  'orcapen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk.git@49e539fd59f3224ecda965d777c7ec3aadcc3b85'
```

<span id="check-the-installation"></span>`uv` creates the environment in `.venv` and records the exact revision of every
dependency in `uv.lock`. Check the installation:

```bash
uv run python -c 'import scgsim; from importlib.metadata import version; print(version("scgsim"))'
```

Check: the command prints `3.0.0rc4` without an import error.

## 3. Choose the extras {#extras}

The words in brackets after `scgsim` are its extras: optional parts that bring
the libraries one kind of work needs. Without an extra, SCGSim reads returned
results only.

| Extra | What it adds | Install it to |
|---|---|---|
| `palace` | GDSFactory, Gmsh, gdstk, Shapely | build a layout's 3D model, check it and mesh it for Palace; [First simulation](first-simulation.qmd) needs it |
| `aedt` | PyAEDT 1.3.0; OCP, the CAD kernel that writes the STEP file AEDT imports; gdstk, Shapely | prepare HFSS, Q3D and Q2D runs and run them in AEDT |
| `aedt-epr` | everything in `aedt`, plus GDSFactory and KLayout | prepare AEDT runs from a GDSFactory layout, as the [Q3D](../guides/capacitance-q3d.qmd) and [HPC sweep](../guides/hpc-sweep.qmd) guides do |
| `visualization` | PyVista, meshio, Pillow | [preview the geometry](../guides/preview-the-geometry.qmd) and look at a prepared model and its mesh |

<span id="add-a-backend-extra"></span>To add an extra later, run `uv add` again with every extra you want; `uv` keeps
the pinned tag:

```bash
uv add 'scgsim[palace,aedt] @ git+https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim.git@v3.0.0rc4'
```

## 4. Install Palace {#palace}

SCGSim prepares runs for stock [Palace 0.18.1](https://awslabs.github.io/palace/stable/install/);
install it on the computer that runs them. SCGSim does not search for Palace:
your script passes the Palace command to `prepare_handoff(executable=...)`,
which writes it into the run script `run_palace.sh`. The guides read that
command from the environment variable `SCGSIM_PALACE_EXECUTABLE`, which you set
in the shell where you run them, as [First simulation](first-simulation.qmd#palace-executable)
does:

```bash
export SCGSIM_PALACE_EXECUTABLE="$(command -v palace)"
```

[Run a prepared model](../guides/run-elsewhere.qmd) covers MPI, schedulers and
running on another computer.

## 5. AEDT {#aedt}

AEDT runs need Ansys Electronics Desktop 2023.2 or 2024.2 and its license on
the computer that runs them; each AEDT request names its version with
`aedt_version="2023.2"` or `"2024.2"`. Both versions use PyAEDT 1.3.0, which
the `aedt` extra installs; AEDT itself is not a Python package.

## Pair SCGSim with the PDK {#pair-with-the-pdk}

SCGSim `3.0.0rc4` pairs with the OrcaPen SC PDK at revision
[`49e539f`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk/tree/49e539fd59f3224ecda965d777c7ec3aadcc3b85),
the one above: version `1.0.0`, installed as `orcapen-sc-pdk` and imported as
`orcapen_sc_pdk`, with GDSFactory 9.48. When an example names another
revision, use the one it names, and keep each study's revisions in its
`uv.lock`.

The [historical Circular Pad setup](../contribute/history/curved-source-installation.qmd)
pins its own SCGSim, PDK and Palace revisions; use them only to reproduce that
run. The PDK revisions it and the guides of SCGSim `2.0.0rc11` name use the
package's earlier names, `orpen-sc-pdk` and `orpen_sc_pdk`.

## Rebuild the environment on another computer

Keep `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` with the study. On another computer, run `uv sync` in the project directory to recreate the locked environment:

```bash
uv sync
```
